observations.body: The speaker asks for deliverance, says God does not delight in sacrifice alone, names a broken spirit, and then anticipates righteous offerings in restored Zion.
observations.label: A broken spirit comes before restored sacrifices

observations.body: The passage presents bloodguilt, praise, broken spirit, divine favor, rebuilt walls, and future offerings as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: bloodguilt, praise, broken spirit, divine favor, rebuilt walls, and future offerings

observations.body: The passage places contrition and restoration beside bloodguilt, praise, broken spirit, divine favor, rebuilt walls, and future offerings.

payload.posture: Read Psalms 51:14–19 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the psalm places inner contrition and later offerings in sequence rather than choosing only one
payload.title: A broken spirit comes before restored sacrifices
